When people are required to pay for something, the makers tend to care less about the quality of it.

I once had an introductory thermodynamics text where the image for the introductory chapter on the second law (the one about increasing entropy) was a toddler. Took my little one getting to be two years old before I got it.

Maybe textbook authors are just wittier than you realize?

In the case of your O'Reily book, animal sketches are just a tradition of theirs.

Speaking from my experience in the industry, when you see a wacky cover like that, 90% of the time it's because the primadonna author insisted on it and the publisher caved because the author's one of their speshul snoflayke darlings. And 99% of the time, if the author insists on a hideous or stupid cover, it's because it was their own photo/artwork or because they've imagined some convoluted allegory related to the image that they think is clever.

Authors. Don't even get me started.

The other 10% of the time that you get a wacky cover like that, it's because nobody in the company who was working on the book could agree on what the cover should be, so they ended up, inevitably, with a cover nobody liked.
